title: Dry Season
blurb: The wells have failed and a heat wave is rolling in. The supply wagon with the spare pump valve went over the edge: ride down, fetch the valve from the wreck, fit it to a well, and hold three hot nights.

objective.text: Fetch the Pump Valve from the Canyon Floor and Fit It to a Well

telegram.title: The Wells Have Failed
telegram.body: WELLS FAILING ACROSS THE GULCH STOP HEAT WAVE INBOUND STOP SUPPLY WAGON WITH THE SPARE PUMP VALVE WENT OVER THE EDGE STOP IT LIES ON THE FLOOR BY A TUNNEL STOP RIDE DOWN FETCH IT FIT IT TO A WELL STOP HOLD THREE NIGHTS STOP

build: Your pump valves cracked in the heat. Every well's bone dry till you fit a new one.
Spare valve was on the supply wagon. The wagon went over the edge. Take the rope down.
wave: Hold them off. No water, no crops. No crops, no supper.

build: Heat wave's coming. I'm selling ice at the casino. It's mostly water. Mostly.
Those wells didn't crack in the heat. I looked at mine. Somebody fitted a railroad seal on the pipe.
wave: Hundred and ten in the shade. Turrets run hot. Pace your shots.

build: Barrels warp in this heat. The Board approves, so long as they warp upward.
That supply wagon was stencilled 'Amber Survey Stores'. Whatever amber is, the railroad's surveying for it.
wave: Last night of the heat. Keep that water flowing.

drop: Wagon's wrecked by a tunnel mouth. Valve's in the back. Mind what lives in tunnels.
pickup: Careful with that. It's the last good valve this side of Tucson. Railroad stencil on that wagon, too.
delivered: Valve's fitted. The pumps are drinking again. Fine plumbing, ranchers.
reminder: That valve's still down in the canyon. The wells won't wait forever.
up: Valve's out of the canyon. Now get it to a well.
hold: Wave's done, but nobody's fitted that valve. Down the rope and get it!
win: Three dry nights held and the wells are flowing. Drinks are on Pearl.
lost: The heat took a house. Dust yourselves off. We'll try it again.

journal.title: Specimen Notes, No. 2
journal.body:
The bugs climb harder when the wells run low. They follow water up the rock like roots grown backwards.

The ranchers' wagon came from a railroad survey party: tents, picks, and crates marked AMBER SURVEY STORES. Nobody surveys a canyon they mean to leave alone.

- E. Whitlow, Rail Car 9

headline_win: Wells Flow Again; Mesa Ranchers Beat the Heat
headline_loss: Mesa Goes Dry; Valve Still in Canyon Wreck
